Number Plate Cloning 2

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go undercover and expose both legal and illegal number plate embossers, but we also look at the number plate industry - regulation problems - and how it effects the consumer.

Summary:
Did you know 4 out of every 10 number plates is cloned? We go undercover and are able to get number plates from a sign shop and a legally permitted embosser. There are over 400 different types of number plates out there, last year SABS wanted to clamp down and make a national plate that is easier to police and catch those who are going to embossers and cloning plates. How does this effect the person sitting at home? Well this could be you, we speak with case studies who have had eToll fines, traffic fines and even been accused of murder and robbery - all victims of number plate cloning. Not only that, but we look at the legal industry and their difficulties with SABS and their regulations which aren't working.

Further information:
Elmarie Jordan - case study: This just happened to us today, we went to renew our cars license at the Post Office and was told it is not possible to renew the license, as this car was stolen! I assured them that the car is most definitely not stolen and never was stolen. Then the nightmare began!
Further Details: I am so frustrated! Apparently the car was stolen on 25 March 2015, marked as murder, robbery and hijacking on the system! From Post Office to Randburg Licensing Department to Langlaagte Licensing Department! Eventually a VERY friendly gentlemen helped us, R600 cash upfront, took the car to have all the numbers sprayed and marked so the car can now show as being a recovered stolen vehicle! Now we have to go back tomorrow for a clearance certificate! According to Langlaagte License Department, this is the correct way to do it!!! This is just unbelievable, this is fraud! The car was never stolen, surely this must be investigated and reported at a police station, but no, the car must be dotted and listed as a recovered stolen vehicle and I must pay for all this and still no license! Very interested to see how many fines we are going to receive and of course the e-toll account is standing at R3000. UNBELIEVABLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Jerry Rekhotso - case study: An embosser who has had many problems in starting his legal business: "To sum up in short the kind of service I received from SABS , I will say to you that nobody deserves to be treated like the way they treated me more especially in our so called new South Africa . I am really still waiting patiently because I want the business and I have already spend a lot of money to open this business . I am paying R 5000 pm for the premises I rented , I am paying someone a monthly salary for doing nothing because of the systems SABS is employing to get my application approved. Their system is pathetic and outdated. Their system reminds me of the South Africa that I grew into as a young boy . We cant go back there.

I began this process of applying for number plate permit in 2014. I received an application on 11/04/2014 and received a quote from SABS on 04/09/2014. I am sorry I cannot remember the date I paid , but from the emails I send you , you will pick up when I send back proof of payment to them . I am still waiting and hoping one day Mr. Johan Gouws will feel emphathy for me and send me my SAN number so that I carry on with my business. I do not know how to beg SABS to finalize my application. I have lost over R60 000 already for the business that is not operational , because of the so called systems by SABS."

Will get a third case study from wayne duvenage showing the e-toll bills that are high and traffic fines, my first case study has all three of these things.
Please see the other two case studies - in which we have filmed undercover.

Outa put out a request for people to come forward about cloned number plates, and recieved THOUSANDS of complaints. Not only that, but they say they have had over 200,000 emails regarding cloned number plates since sanral began eTolls.
We have undercover footage from both places.

more case studies:
EXTRA CASE STUDY’S FROM OUTA:
Alan Schutz My mother was sent an incorrect e-toll bill. On their invoice it had a picture of the vehicle and registration number. The registration number was the same as my mother's vehicle, but the picture of the cloned number plate was a Putco bus. My mother is a 70 year old pensioner and was now expected to try and get this resolved. It was eventually resolved with some aggravation, and my sister getting involved. To resolve this takes time and money running around. Whether you're a pensioner or lucky enough to be employed, it costs the general public to try and resolve their mistakes. Economic pressures are all around us, why should this obviously faulty system place further economic pressures on the public?
I've been keeping an eye on a lot of the commentary regarding e-tolls. But I have not seen anything regarding how unemployed individuals are expected to pay e-tolls (across all racial lines, not that racial lines should have anything to do with it). Should they rather be paying e-tolls or contributing to putting food on the table. Or are they to be banned from totally using public e-tolled routes?
Anthon Walters Hi I have two vehicles operating in Durban, one BMW 320i and a KIA Rio. There is two vehicles a Mercedes E class and a Honda operating with these two vehicles number plates in Gauteng. Total bill about R7500-00.
Leon Hannibal Cell: +27(0)82 880 8401, email: leon@hannibal.org.za
My wife's bill is around R6k or so and we get photos of her current car (Hyundai iX35) and her previous car (Toyota Yaris) with the same number plates and we changed cars in March 2012! On that basis, I am challenging the legitimacy of any of my bills. I want a photo of each and every gantry pass before I part with one cent!

From: "Steve Admin"
I had a woman phone me one day screaming that I had COPIED HER registration number and plates to avoid paying e tolls . I do not pay E tolls at all and have never registered.
After many e mails back and forth it transpired that she had received a bill for A white Toyota Bakkie like mine with her registration on it ???
I eventually asked her to send me the photo from E toll , Low and behold the vehicle in the picture was mine BUT the plates were the genuine ones and the number had been miss identified by the gantry. The Toll Gantry had miss read the photo and sent her the bill in Error ??
I have no idea if she managed to get the Toll fee credited unfortunately
Steve Hurley

Press Release:


Plate Cloning Chaos
Over 350 different types of licence plates are legal in South Africa and it’s estimated that one in five plates on Gauteng roads is cloned. Just how easy is it to buy and use illegal number plates? As our undercover cameras expose the clone cons, Carte Blanche also gets exclusive access to a new JMPD methodology that stops drivers with cloned or illegal number plates in their tracks


Script:


At the Johannesburg Metro Police Department Headquarters, a computer programme is scanning South Africa’s roads and processing thousands of vehicles, searching for cloned number plates. It’s called the Central Joint Information Project, and is a government classified project established for the Hawks in 2007. It takes the eNatis and S-A-P-S vehicle hot lists and compares them with other vehicle sightings in the so-called “fish pond.” Using advanced recognition software and existing cameras on highways or shopping centre parking lots, a vehicles’ registration number and, even its make, can be identified. With a success rate of about 30 prosecutions a month, the project’s potential to curb fraud seems promising.
Gerrie: “It will catch up with you, because JMPD will get hold of you.”
Gerrie Gerneke is the director of the JMPDs specialized number plate cloning division. He’s made it his mission to find those who commit crimes using illegal or false number plates - even those changing or obscuring a digit to avoid paying traffic fines or eToll bills.
Gerrie: “We can pin point the vehicle using GPS co-ordinates where the cloned plates that are travelling around in JHB.”
LINK – THE LAW IS CLEAR, IT’S YOUR RESPONSIBILITY TO MAKE SURE THAT THIS PLATE, MATCHES THE DETAILS ON YOUR LICENSE DISK.
SHOW CAR EXAMPLE: These are similar cars, but they have the same number plates. However, this car was spotted 306 kilometers away, 41 minutes later. The computer figured out in order for it to be the same car, it would have had to have travelled an impossible 743 kilometres per hour.
When Carte Blanche asked for viewer accounts of cloned plates, the public responded...
Many had similar complaints to this 82-year old grandmother, whose number plate was cloned and she was forced to contest nearly 16-thousand rand in traffic fines. The JMPD linked the owner of THIS fiat panda to her cloned plate. The car has since been impounded and the police hope to make an arrest soon.
So far clone matches have resulted in a 40% successful arrest rate.
LINK: A NUMBER PLATE IS NOT JUST A NUMBER PLATE, THERE ARE ABOUT 350 VARIATIONS AND IN GAUTENG, THANKS TO ETOLLS, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT 1 IN 5 ARE CLONED.
Another victim of cloning is Kim Hawker. She owns Zonke Tours - a shuttle bus business -with several Hyundai vans like this one. She registered for eTags. Three months later, she received a bill for a bakkie that was not hers but had the same registration. “When she queried it with SANRAL, she got through to “Philip.”
SOUND UP: “Speaking to Philip...”
She believes this was the same Phillip made famous by Johannesburg Radio Talk Show Host Darren “Whackhead” Simpson.
Darren: “hi, is this the violation centre?”
He called on behalf of a motorist who had a very unlikely bill of R434 thousand.
Whackhead: “That would mean he would have had to go around the ring 170 times per day.”
Philip: “I just hang up the phone.”
Kim said Philip ALSO hung up on her, and after that, she refused to pay
In March THIS year, she received an eToll bill for 80,000 rand. Her bill also incorrectly stated that she is not registered.
Kim: “I panicked to begin with, there have been problems in the past, cloned, no response. Don’t carry passengers in a bakkie... be out of business.”
Then in early July, she got a nasty surprise when another one of her vehicles had allegedly been involved in a robbery in Garsfontein, Pretoria.
Kim: “Two detectives knocked on the door, and told us the registration was involved in robbery. I do have a schedule, I was picking up clients from airport.”
Kim made a statement and said the police accepted her explanation. However, her number plate is still associated with the robbery.
Kim: “I could be arrested.”
Carmen Jordan is a 21-year old law student in Pretoria. When she went to renew her car license last month she got the shock of her life.
Carmen: “They said my car was used in a robbery, hijacking and murder case.”
As the vehicle belongs to her parents, they had to fly in from Dubai where they live to try and resolve the matter. R20 000 and four days later, like Kim, Carmen’s number plate is still associated with a crime - this time murder.
Carmen: “My life is in danger, if I just drove away from the police, let’s say I didn’t hear the sirens or I didn’t stop, they could just shoot on me.”
Carmen ALSO received an eToll bill worth R3000, however the tricky cloners used an identical make-of-car to hers.
Carmen: “That’s why the eTag is such a problem right now, because it’s my car and my number plate that they see, but it’s not actually.”
SANRAL SAID THEY ARE NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLONING OF NUMBER PLATES, AND THERE’S ONLY BEEN A SLIGHT INCREASE SINCE THE INCEPTION OF ETOLLS. THEIR SOFTWARE PICKS UP AROUND 2000 POTENTIALLY CLONED VEHICLES, WHICH ARE PLACED ON A CLONED VEHICLE LIST. HOWEVER, THE BURDEN IS UPON THE ROAD USER TO “PROVE” THAT THEIR NUMBER PLATE HAS BEEN CLONED. ACCORDING TO SANRAL AN ETAG IS LINKED TO YOUR NUMBER PLATE AND THEREFORE THEY CAN PICK UP IF THE DRIVER IS NOT YOU.
Gerrie’s team of 12 officers and four “smart road-block” vehicles are fitted with advanced number plate scanning software that’s connected to their computer system at headquarters. They make illegal number plate hot lists and use these to identify law breakers in REAL TIME.
UPSOUND: Police: “This vehicle was written off by insurance, and now it was taken off the system.”
The JMPD gave Carte Blanche exclusive access to see their technology in action over several days.
When this McClaren was pulled over, the driver was forced to remove the dealership plates. And when they took a closer look at his permit...
UPSOUND: Police: “He doesn’t have a roadworthy for the vehicle, so he doesn’t qualify for the permit, which means that that permit is fraudulent.”
This motorcyclist was spotted in traffic. He was using a trade plate outside of the allowed trading hours. He’d also blacked out the middle digits.
This man was caught using his old number plate.
UPSOUND: Police: “These fines are going to the current owner. Your number plate is previously used.”
Gerrie blames the number plate cloning conundrum on the ease with which you can buy a cloned plate.
LINK: THERE IS NO LACK OF RULES OR REGULATIONS WHEN IT COMES TO NUMBER PLATES, THERE ARE DETAILED STANDARDS FOR MANUFACTURES OF THE BLANK PLATES, BUT ALSO FOR THE EMBOSSERS THAT PUT ON THE REGISTRATION NUMBERS, THE PROBLEM IS POLICING THOSE LAWS.
Zurika Louw of the South Africa Number Plates Association went undercover with Carte Blanche and bought several number plates from Big 2 – an SABS permitted store in Johannesburg central.
Zurika: “They are making number plates without proper identification.”
Zurika: "I am thinking now, a friend of mine needs one for their bikes.”
Guy: “Yes we can make it.”
He prints the number plates and returns in minutes.
Zurika: “I don’t have an ID.”
Guy: “Do you have?”
Zurika: “No my ID was stolen and my driver’s licence is in the car.”
Guy: “Okay just write your ID number and your initials.”
And voila! Two cloned plates. One, a legal aluminium, the other a plastic plate. Note the reversed Gauteng Logo.
Frank Makamo, the director for certification at the SABS said Big 2 have broken the law by not making sure the vehicle’s registration number matches the person’s identification and licence disk.
Frank: “Failure to produce these two things, the embosser is not allowed to give you the number plate.”
Zurika visited Arrow Signs in Centurion, where she asked them to make her a number plate.
Lana: “We make something that looks like a real number plate, but they are not legal number plates.”
Zurika: “How much are they?”
Lana: “It’s R200 each.”
Zurika: “The plates look so real.”
Lana: “Yes, if they haven’t got the SABS approval, it’s a sign.”
Despite the fact we were openly told this was not a legal number plate, it could be fraudulently used as one. When asked why it matched the SABS specifications for number plate characteristics exactly, Arrow Signs declined to comment saying the matter was currently before court and therefore sub-judice.
Derek: “Can’t you go check up on them?”
Frank: “As SABS we monitor the quality to the public, but not the selling of the product.”
The SABS mandate only allows it to check up on legal embossers. It is the police who check up on the illegal embossers.
Gerrie: “I think are still a lot of uncertainty on exactly what the law says.”
Zurika said she has reported both Big 2 and Arrow Signs to the SABS.
D: “Where’s the manager?”
G: “I’m here.”
D: “I’m derek from Carte Blanche, we got these number plates made up and it was without any identification...”
G: Who was the person that was making them?
D: Well we got it on camera.
While we were trying to get answers, we were asked to leave.
Derek: “We did phone.”
Guy2: “Get that camera out of my face.”
Derek: “What has this got to do with you.”
Guy 2: “I work here.”
LINK: I get the distinct impression that they don’t want to explain...
Frank agrees that they need to check up on legal embossers like Big 2 more regularly, and said their aim is to have one national number plate with an identification chip.
Frank: “If we can manage to introduce with the department of transport, a single system and a chip system controlled from here.”
Gerrie invites national and local cloning victims to report their cases so they can add them to their hotlist. He said an SABS national number plate will go a long way towards policing illegal number plates.
Gerrie: “We would be big supporters of a central data base with one type of number plate.”
END: 10.15
Could your number plate be cloned and on the police hotlist?
UPSOUND: Carmen: “They said my car was used in a murder, robbery and hijacking case.”
The Johannesburg Metro Police is cracking down on criminals and fraudsters using cloned number plates. Carte Blanche gets exclusive access to see their hi-tech system in action.
UPSOUND: “This permit is fraudulent.”
UPSOUND: Carmen: “They said my car was used in a murder, robbery and hijacking case.”
One out of 5 number plates are cloned to avoid etoll bills or commit a crime. Who sells them and how can you protect yourself?

SHOW CAR EXAMPLE: These are similar cars, but they have the same number plates. However, this car was spotted 306 kilometers away, 41 minutes later. The computer figured out in order for it to be the same car, it would have had to have travelled an impossible 743 kilometres per hour. When Carte Blanche asked for viewer accounts of cloned plates, the public responded... Many had similar complaints to this 82-year old grandmother, whose number plate was cloned and she was forced to contest nearly 16-thousand rand in traffic fines. The JMPD linked the owner of THIS fiat panda to her cloned plate. The car has since been impounded and the police hope to make an arrest soon. So far clone matches have resulted in a 40% successful arrest rate. LINK: A NUMBER PLATE IS NOT JUST A NUMBER PLATE, THERE ARE ABOUT 350 VARIATIONS AND IN GAUTENG, THANKS TO ETOLLS, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT 1 IN 5 ARE CLONED. Another victim of cloning is Kim Hawker. She owns Zonke Tours - a shuttle bus business -with several Hyundai vans like this one. She registered for eTags. Three months later, she received a bill for a bakkie that was not hers but had the same registration. “When she queried it with SANRAL, she got through to “Philip.” SOUND UP: “Speaking to Philip...” She believes this was the same Phillip made famous by Johannesburg Radio Talk Show Host Darren “Whackhead” Simpson. Darren: “hi, is this the violation centre?” He called on behalf of a motorist who had a very unlikely bill of R434 thousand. Whackhead: “That would mean he would have had to go around the ring 170 times per day.” Philip: “I just hang up the phone.” Kim said Philip ALSO hung up on her, and after that, she refused to pay In March THIS year, she received an eToll bill for 80,000 rand. Her bill also incorrectly stated that she is not registered. Kim: “I panicked to begin with, there have been problems in the past, cloned, no response. Don’t carry passengers in a bakkie... be out of business.” Then in early July, she got a nasty surprise when another one of her vehicles had allegedly been involved in a robbery in Garsfontein, Pretoria. Kim: “Two detectives knocked on the door, and told us the registration was involved in robbery. I do have a schedule, I was picking up clients from airport.” Kim made a statement and said the police accepted her explanation. However, her number plate is still associated with the robbery. Kim: “I could be arrested.” Carmen Jordan is a 21-year old law student in Pretoria. When she went to renew her car license last month she got the shock of her life. Carmen: “They said my car was used in a robbery, hijacking and murder case.” As the vehicle belongs to her parents, they had to fly in from Dubai where they live to try and resolve the matter. R20 000 and four days later, like Kim, Carmen’s number plate is still associated with a crime - this time murder. Carmen: “My life is in danger, if I just drove away from the police, let’s say I didn’t hear the sirens or I didn’t stop, they could just shoot on me.” Carmen ALSO received an eToll bill worth R3000, however the tricky cloners used an identical make-of-car to hers. Carmen: “That’s why the eTag is such a problem right now, because it’s my car and my number plate that they see, but it’s not actually.” SANRAL SAID THEY ARE NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CLONING OF NUMBER PLATES, AND THERE’S ONLY BEEN A SLIGHT INCREASE SINCE THE INCEPTION OF ETOLLS. THEIR SOFTWARE PICKS UP AROUND 2000 POTENTIALLY CLONED VEHICLES, WHICH ARE PLACED ON A CLONED VEHICLE LIST. HOWEVER, THE BURDEN IS UPON THE ROAD USER TO “PROVE” THAT THEIR NUMBER PLATE HAS BEEN CLONED. ACCORDING TO SANRAL AN ETAG IS LINKED TO YOUR NUMBER PLATE AND THEREFORE THEY CAN PICK UP IF THE DRIVER IS NOT YOU. Gerrie’s team of 12 officers and four “smart road-block” vehicles are fitted with advanced number plate scanning software that’s connected to their computer system at headquarters. They make illegal number plate hot lists and use these to identify law breakers in REAL TIME. UPSOUND: Police: “This vehicle was written off by insurance, and now it was taken off the system.” The JMPD gave Carte Blanche exclusive access to see their technology in action over several days. When this McClaren was pulled over, the driver was forced to remove the dealership plates. And when they took a closer look at his permit... UPSOUND: Police: “He doesn’t have a roadworthy for the vehicle, so he doesn’t qualify for the permit, which means that that permit is fraudulent.” This motorcyclist was spotted in traffic. He was using a trade plate outside of the allowed trading hours. He’d also blacked out the middle digits. This man was caught using his old number plate. UPSOUND: Police: “These fines are going to the current owner. Your number plate is previously used.” Gerrie blames the number plate cloning conundrum on the ease with which you can buy a cloned plate. LINK: THERE IS NO LACK OF RULES OR REGULATIONS WHEN IT COMES TO NUMBER PLATES, THERE ARE DETAILED STANDARDS FOR MANUFACTURES OF THE BLANK PLATES, BUT ALSO FOR THE EMBOSSERS THAT PUT ON THE REGISTRATION NUMBERS, THE PROBLEM IS POLICING THOSE LAWS. Zurika Louw of the South Africa Number Plates Association went undercover with Carte Blanche and bought several number plates from Big 2 – an SABS permitted store in Johannesburg central. Zurika: “They are making number plates without proper identification.” Zurika: "I am thinking now, a friend of mine needs one for their bikes.” Guy: “Yes we can make it.” He prints the number plates and returns in minutes. Zurika: “I don’t have an ID.” Guy: “Do you have?” Zurika: “No my ID was stolen and my driver’s licence is in the car.” Guy: “Okay just write your ID number and your initials.” And voila! Two cloned plates. One, a legal aluminium, the other a plastic plate. Note the reversed Gauteng Logo. Frank Makamo, the director for certification at the SABS said Big 2 have broken the law by not making sure the vehicle’s registration number matches the person’s identification and licence disk. Frank: “Failure to produce these two things, the embosser is not allowed to give you the number plate.” Zurika visited Arrow Signs in Centurion, where she asked them to make her a number plate. Lana: “We make something that looks like a real number plate, but they are not legal number plates.” Zurika: “How much are they?” Lana: “It’s R200 each.” Zurika: “The plates look so real.” Lana: “Yes, if they haven’t got the SABS approval, it’s a sign.” Despite the fact we were openly told this was not a legal number plate, it could be fraudulently used as one. When asked why it matched the SABS specifications for number plate characteristics exactly, Arrow Signs declined to comment saying the matter was currently before court and therefore sub-judice. Derek: “Can’t you go check up on them?” Frank: “As SABS we monitor the quality to the public, but not the selling of the product.” The SABS mandate only allows it to check up on legal embossers. It is the police who check up on the illegal embossers. Gerrie: “I think are still a lot of uncertainty on exactly what the law says.” Zurika said she has reported both Big 2 and Arrow Signs to the SABS. D: “Where’s the manager?” G: “I’m here.” D: “I’m derek from Carte Blanche, we got these number plates made up and it was without any identification...” G: Who was the person that was making them? D: Well we got it on camera. While we were trying to get answers, we were asked to leave. Derek: “We did phone.” Guy2: “Get that camera out of my face.” Derek: “What has this got to do with you.” Guy 2: “I work here.” LINK: I get the distinct impression that they don’t want to explain... Frank agrees that they need to check up on legal embossers like Big 2 more regularly, and said their aim is to have one national number plate with an identification chip. Frank: “If we can manage to introduce with the department of transport, a single system and a chip system controlled from here.” Gerrie invites national and local cloning victims to report their cases so they can add them to their hotlist. He said an SABS national number plate will go a long way towards policing illegal number plates. Gerrie: “We would be big supporters of a central data base with one type of number plate.” END: 10.15 Could your number plate be cloned and on the police hotlist? UPSOUND: Carmen: “They said my car was used in a murder, robbery and hijacking case.” The Johannesburg Metro Police is cracking down on criminals and fraudsters using cloned number plates. Carte Blanche gets exclusive access to see their hi-tech system in action. UPSOUND: “This permit is fraudulent.” UPSOUND: Carmen: “They said my car was used in a murder, robbery and hijacking case.” One out of 5 number plates are cloned to avoid etoll bills or commit a crime. Who sells them and how can you protect yourself? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We go undercover and expose both legal and illegal number plate embossers, but we also look at the number plate industry - regulation problems - and how it effects the consumer.
metadata.Summary: Did you know 4 out of every 10 number plates is cloned? We go undercover and are able to get number plates from a sign shop and a legally permitted embosser. There are over 400 different types of number plates out there, last year SABS wanted to clamp down and make a national plate that is easier to police and catch those who are going to embossers and cloning plates. How does this effect the person sitting at home? Well this could be you, we speak with case studies who have had eToll fines, traffic fines and even been accused of murder and robbery - all victims of number plate cloning. Not only that, but we look at the legal industry and their difficulties with SABS and their regulations which aren't working.
metadata.Further information: Elmarie Jordan - case study: This just happened to us today, we went to renew our cars license at the Post Office and was told it is not possible to renew the license, as this car was stolen! I assured them that the car is most definitely not stolen and never was stolen. Then the nightmare began! Further Details: I am so frustrated! Apparently the car was stolen on 25 March 2015, marked as murder, robbery and hijacking on the system! From Post Office to Randburg Licensing Department to Langlaagte Licensing Department! Eventually a VERY friendly gentlemen helped us, R600 cash upfront, took the car to have all the numbers sprayed and marked so the car can now show as being a recovered stolen vehicle! Now we have to go back tomorrow for a clearance certificate! According to Langlaagte License Department, this is the correct way to do it!!! This is just unbelievable, this is fraud! The car was never stolen, surely this must be investigated and reported at a police station, but no, the car must be dotted and listed as a recovered stolen vehicle and I must pay for all this and still no license! Very interested to see how many fines we are going to receive and of course the e-toll account is standing at R3000. UNBELIEVABLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Jerry Rekhotso - case study: An embosser who has had many problems in starting his legal business: "To sum up in short the kind of service I received from SABS , I will say to you that nobody deserves to be treated like the way they treated me more especially in our so called new South Africa . I am really still waiting patiently because I want the business and I have already spend a lot of money to open this business . I am paying R 5000 pm for the premises I rented , I am paying someone a monthly salary for doing nothing because of the systems SABS is employing to get my application approved. Their system is pathetic and outdated. Their system reminds me of the South Africa that I grew into as a young boy . We cant go back there. I began this process of applying for number plate permit in 2014. I received an application on 11/04/2014 and received a quote from SABS on 04/09/2014. I am sorry I cannot remember the date I paid , but from the emails I send you , you will pick up when I send back proof of payment to them . I am still waiting and hoping one day Mr. Johan Gouws will feel emphathy for me and send me my SAN number so that I carry on with my business. I do not know how to beg SABS to finalize my application. I have lost over R60 000 already for the business that is not operational , because of the so called systems by SABS." Will get a third case study from wayne duvenage showing the e-toll bills that are high and traffic fines, my first case study has all three of these things. Please see the other two case studies - in which we have filmed undercover. Outa put out a request for people to come forward about cloned number plates, and recieved THOUSANDS of complaints. Not only that, but they say they have had over 200,000 emails regarding cloned number plates since sanral began eTolls. We have undercover footage from both places. more case studies: EXTRA CASE STUDY’S FROM OUTA: Alan Schutz
